clue.text: Eagle perhaps? Not quite

blocks.note: surface reading: a large bird of prey, offered as an example of something
setter's reading: in golf an eagle is two under par, and the score that falls just short of it is one under

explanation.surface: Someone guesses an eagle and then hedges.
explanation.walkthrough: The eagle looks like a bird to name, but it is the golf score; the answer is the golf score one stroke worse, and also a little bird, which keeps the bird surface honest.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a birdie is one stroke under par, just short of the two-under eagle.

clue.text: Cooked beef’s first up

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: opening letter of the meat
raised means lifted up

explanation.surface: A cook reports that the beef was put on first.
explanation.definitionFit: Braising is a way of cooking meat slowly in a little liquid, so braised describes food cooked that way.

clue.text: Alan Shearer’s forsaken an evil practice

indicators.note: to forsake is to abandon, so the named letters are dropped from the footballer's name
something evil is corrupt or twisted, so the remaining letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: the footballer's full name taken as letters
the two letters to remove

explanation.surface: A famous striker has abandoned some wicked training habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a former England centre-forward. Take one A and the N out of his name and rearrange the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run of a performance before the real thing.

clue.text: Patient batting partner

blocks.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A cricketer waits calmly while their partner bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' reads as an adjective about the batsman; it is a noun, someone held in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a person confined in an institution, such as a patient detained in a psychiatric hospital.

clue.text: Even so, this a tad cryptic?

indicators.note: cryptic means coded or obscured, so the letters are disguised by being put in another order

blocks.note: the three words taken as letters

explanation.surface: A solver wonders whether this clue is a little too obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases concede a point before qualifying it: 'nevertheless', 'however'.

clue.text: Person who succeeds welcomed by the Irish

indicators.note: something welcomed by a group is taken inside it, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A successful person is warmly received by the people of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeds' suggests doing well; here it means taking over from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the one who inherits a title or estate, succeeding the previous holder.

clue.text: Cheek still turned, worth poking that

indicators.note: turned round means the word is read the other way
poking into something means pushing inside it, so this goes into the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: still in the sense of 'yet', as in 'still to come'
merit is worth

explanation.surface: Someone turns a cheek while a valuable thing pokes into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to the reversed piece: the worth word pokes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is audacious boldness, the same impudence as cheek.

clue.text: Navy at bottom of a party dress

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the end, so this piece is placed after the others

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor turns up at the end of a party wearing a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress something, like a shop window, is to decorate it, which is to adorn it.

clue.text: What might make bedroom cold for rodents?

blocks.note: a dorm is a shared bedroom
ice is cold

explanation.surface: A question about what chills a bedroom for small animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormice are small, mostly nocturnal rodents famous for hibernating.

clue.text: In a book, husband parts

indicators.note: parts here is a verb, splitting the book apart so the other piece sits between

blocks.note: taken as written
a tome is a large book
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A man appears in a book in several parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun for sections of the book; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in is to be at home, as in 'Is she in?'

clue.text: Picture lover from Italian capital with leg wound

indicators.note: a capital is the head letter of a word, so only the initial is used
wound as in twisted round, so the letters are wound into a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: An art fan from Rome has an injured leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' seems to be a link word but is part of the fodder; 'Italian capital' wants to be Rome, but is just its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film in everyday speech, so someone who loves pictures is a cinema-goer.

clue.text: Source of energy in sprout for bird

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a bud is a sprout on a plant
a star such as the sun radiates energy

explanation.surface: A sprout is offered as a power food for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bustard is a large, heavy ground-dwelling game bird of open plains.

clue.text: Craft beer’s drunk – get away!

indicators.note: the beer has drunk the craft, taking it inside itself

blocks.note: stout is a dark beer
a craft is an art or skill

explanation.surface: Someone has downed a craft ale and is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft beer' is a single idea on the surface; split it, and the apostrophe-s means 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To start out is to set off on a journey, which is what getting away does.

clue.text: Character entering Burundi after vacation, small nation

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied of its contents, leaving only its outside letters
entering means going inside, so this piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the country name with its middle emptied
a rune is a character of an old alphabet

explanation.surface: A figure arrives in one African country on returning from holiday, small as it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' reads as a holiday; here it means emptying out. One country hides another.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is a tiny sultanate on the island of Borneo, a small state.

clue.text: Low vehicle I’d entered in competitions, reversing up

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is turned round
entered in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: races are competitions
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone admits to entering a low-slung car in races and backing it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is the small low passenger carriage attached to the side of a motorcycle.

clue.text: Food served, a beauty

blocks.note: first meaning: a course or item of food brought to the table
second meaning: informal for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A waiter brings out a meal that looks gorgeous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a prepared item of food and, in slang, a good-looking person.

clue.text: A priest set about erotic performance

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the three words taken as letters

explanation.surface: A clergyman has begun some saucy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is an entertainment in which a performer slowly undresses, an erotic act.

clue.text: Farmer in contrary gardener removing hat for military unit

indicators.note: a hat is worn on top, and in a down entry the top is the first letter, which comes off
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow?'
a tiller is one who tills the soil

explanation.surface: A farmer and a stubborn gardener, the gardener taking off a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The gardener is Mary from the English nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary', who is asked how her garden grows; without her first letter she holds the farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The artillery is the branch of an army that fires big guns, a military formation.

clue.text: Neat hand

blocks.note: first meaning: of a drink, taken undiluted
second meaning: in poker, five cards in sequence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat hand' reads as tidy handwriting; the words are separate, one about drinks and one about cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat whisky is served without water or ice, and in poker a run of five consecutive cards is a named hand.

clue.text: Arctic country’s complete withdrawal

blocks.note: arctic means freezing
a country

explanation.surface: A polar nation pulls out entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Going cold turkey means stopping an addictive drug abruptly and totally, with the withdrawal that follows.

clue.text: Yellow meat

blocks.note: first meaning: cowardly
second meaning: the flesh of a common farm bird

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow meat' sounds like a description of poultry; the colour word means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow and the answer are both slang for cowardly, and the answer is also a common white meat.

clue.text: Male getting leg shortened

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a leg of a journey or race is a stage

explanation.surface: A man has a leg amputated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' looks bodily, but it is the part of a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and by extension a man without a female partner, as on a stag night.

clue.text: Setter spinning yarn in trap

indicators.note: spinning turns something round, so the word runs backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a gin is a snare for game
a yarn is a story

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler spins a tall story into a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to be the crossword's compiler; it is something that makes a liquid set. 'spinning yarn' also hints at wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is used to make jellies and desserts set firm, so it is a setting agent.

clue.text: African rule written in brief letters

definitions.note: the clue gives an adjective; the answer is the country

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter goes
something written in a document is included inside it

blocks.note: mail is letters sent by post
a law is a rule

explanation.surface: An African regulation is set down in a short note.
explanation.definitionFit: Malawi is a landlocked country in south-east Africa, so it is an African state.

clue.text: Passageway suggested? Absolutely!

blocks.note: a passage between rows of seats, pronounced like the contraction
say means suggest, as in 'shall we say noon?'

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a route and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The passageway is spoken rather than spelt: it is pronounced exactly as the contraction for 'I will'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic exclamations of agreement, like 'definitely!' or 'you bet!'

clue.text: Flower: name coming up touring India

indicators.note: in a down entry coming up means reading from the bottom, so the word is turned round
touring means going round, so this piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: to name something is to call it
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A flower's name rises to fame while touring India.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub bearing fragrant purple or white blossoms, a flower.

clue.text: Friend keeping slowing, vehicle ultimately running alongside

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter only
keeping means holding, so the friend wraps around what follows

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
rall. is the musical abbreviation of rallentando, meaning slowing down
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A friend keeps slowing down, the car eventually running next to them.
explanation.walkthrough: Rall., short for rallentando, is the musical direction to slow down gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel lines or roads run side by side, always at the same distance apart.

clue.text: Weakest man, hand on heart in earnest

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letter is used

blocks.note: a paw is informal for a hand
middle letter of the seven

explanation.surface: A feeble man earnestly puts his hand on his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' here is a chess piece, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the lowest-value piece is the pawn, the weakest of the men on the board.

clue.text: Unit of mass I record in retro symbol

indicators.note: retro means backwards-looking, so the word is read the other way
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a mark is a symbol
taken as written
a log is a record

explanation.surface: Someone notes down a weight inside an old-fashioned sign.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilogram is the SI base unit for measuring mass, a thousand grams.

clue.text: Mother for example has father in pieces

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
rent means torn apart

explanation.surface: Mum has smashed Dad to bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is one kind of parent, so she is an example of the category.

clue.text: Drug: figure inhaling it catching cold, half gone

indicators.note: half gone means half the word is lost, keeping only its first two letters
inhaling means breathing in, so the figure takes the rest inside
catching means trapping, so the second piece is held within the first

blocks.note: nine is a number
taken as written
the word taken as written before half of it goes

explanation.surface: Someone smokes and catches a chill, half wasted on a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the shortened cold sits inside 'it', and that whole piece goes inside the number. 'inhaling' fits the smoking surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the addictive stimulant in tobacco, a drug.

clue.text: Leaders in Luxembourg and Italy near an African

indicators.note: leaders are what come first, so only the opening letters are taken

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
by means near, as in 'stand by me'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heads of two European states sit beside an African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' looks like part of the definition; it supplies letters, and the definition is the single word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Libyan is a person from Libya, a North African country, so an African.
